mainTopic: The time of the afternoon תמיד on שבת and ערב פסח (אביי, רבא, רבה בר עולא), and the rule that the two תמידים open and close the day's offerings
overview: The גמרא continues the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about when the afternoon תמיד is brought on שבת. Following רבא's reading, it asks why רבי עקיבא does not bring the תמיד at six and a half hours. It answers that the מוספין (six hours) and the בזיכין (seven hours) must come first, which pushes the תמיד to seven and a half. רבה בר עולא objects that the ברייתא never mentions ערב פסח. He rereads it as an argument about an ordinary שבת, so our משנה about ערב פסח fits everyone, and the argument is about a גזירה on שבת because of the weekday's נדרים and נדבות. Two more ברייתות then test אביי and רבא, and each אמורא defends himself by rereading one phrase. Next a ברייתא teaches that nothing comes before the morning תמיד (רבא: from 'העולה') and nothing comes after the afternoon תמיד. For that second rule, רבא rejects אביי's proof and reads 'השלמים' as 'השלם': all offerings are completed by the afternoon תמיד. The amud ends with a ברייתא giving the ערב פסח order: תמיד, פסח, קטורת, then נרות. The discussion of that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not bring the תמיד at six and a half hours?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's timing. If the earlier worry does not apply, the תמיד could be brought even earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we are not worried, let him bring it at six and a half hours!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי עקיבא's view as רבא explained it. If the earlier concern does not bother him, why not bring the תמיד as early as possible, at six and a half hours?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, רבי עקיבא does not share the worry that led to a later time. Once that worry is gone, nothing seems to stop the תמיד from being brought at six and a half hours, which is the time used when ערב פסח falls on ערב שבת. So why does רבי עקיבא still wait until seven and a half?

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned / we worry about
let him do it (bring the offering)
six and a half hours (the earliest time used for the afternoon תמיד)
the daily communal offering, here the afternoon one

phrases.english: If we are not concerned,
phrases.notes: He means the worry discussed on the previous amud, which רבי עקיבא, as רבא explains him, doesn't share.

phrases.english: let him offer it at six and a half hours!
phrases.notes: The earliest possible time, as on ערב פסח that falls on ערב שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא חָיְישִׁינַן, נִיעְבְּדֵיהּ בְּשֵׁשׁ וּמֶחְצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of רבא's reading of the ברייתא on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's timing of seven and a half hours, as רבא explained it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for a later time does not apply, the תמיד should be brought at the earliest allowed time, six and a half hours.

steps.title: The מוספין and בזיכין come first, pushing the תמיד later
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the מוספין come before the בזיכין. Since both must be done first, the תמיד lands at seven and a half hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the מוספין come before the בזיכין. So he brings the מוספין at six hours, the בזיכין at seven, and the תמיד at seven and a half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a scheduling issue, not the old worry, is what delays the תמיד. On שבת there are other services that must be done first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת there are extra offerings (מוספין) and the bowls of frankincense from the לחם הפנים (בזיכין). רבי עקיבא holds that the מוספין come before the בזיכין. Laid out in order (מוספין at six, בזיכין at seven), the תמיד naturally falls at seven and a half.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds / his view is
the additional offerings of שבת or יום טוב
the bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים and burned on שבת
come first / take precedence

steps.confusionAlert: The delay here does not come from the earlier concern. It comes purely from the order of services that must be done first on שבת.

phrases.english: He holds:
the additional offerings precede the bowls of frankincense.
He offers the additional offerings at six hours,
and the bowls at seven hours,
and he offers the daily offering at seven and a half hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason: the order of services, not the earlier concern, sets the time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the earlier concern, the תמיד could be at six and a half.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the מוספין (six) and then the בזיכין (seven) come first, the תמיד is at seven and a half.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: the ברייתא never mentions ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא attacks the reading shared by אביי and רבא. The words 'on ערב פסח' are not in the ברייתא; it speaks about שבת in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא objected: Does the ברייתא say 'Like its order on a weekday, so is its order on שבת on ערב פסח, says רבי ישמעאל'? It just says 'so is its order on שבת', without adding anything!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא challenges the explanation of the ברייתא given by both אביי and רבא. He says it adds words that are not in the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא both read the ברייתא as talking about a שבת that is ערב פסח. But the ברייתא simply says 'on שבת', with no mention of ערב פסח. So their reading forces an extra detail into the text that is not there.

keyTerms.meaning: he strongly objects to it
an אמורא who challenges רבא's reading
does it teach...? (it doesn't!)
plainly, without qualification
its order or arrangement (here, the timing of the תמיד)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla strongly objected to this:
Does it teach: 'Like its arrangement during the week,
so is its arrangement on Shabbat on Passover eve,
the words of Rabbi Yishmael'?!
It simply teaches: 'so is its arrangement on Shabbat'!
phrases.notes: It's phrased like a question, but the point is that the ברייתא says it plainly, with no exceptions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the scheduling discussion and attacks the textual basis of רבא's whole reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of the ברייתא as dealing with a שבת that is ערב פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says only 'on שבת'. Inserting 'ערב פסח' does not match its plain wording.

steps.title: New reading: רבי ישמעאל compares an ordinary weekday to an ordinary שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא rereads the ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל holds that on an ordinary שבת the תמיד is at the same time as on an ordinary weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר עולא said: This is what it teaches. Like its order on a regular weekday, so is its order on a regular שבת. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבא's reading, רבה בר עולא offers his own. The argument is about an ordinary week, not ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבה בר עולא's reading, רבי ישמעאל says an ordinary שבת is just like an ordinary weekday: the תמיד is at its usual time (eight and a half hours). שבת makes no difference for him.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces a replacement explanation)
this is what it teaches (this is how to read it)
ordinary, of the rest of the year
a weekday

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Ulla said:
This is what it is teaching:
Like its arrangement on an ordinary weekday,
so is its arrangement on an ordinary Shabbat,
phrases.notes: That is, at the regular time of eight and a half hours.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's reading after the objection in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא so it fits its plain wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a שבת that falls on ערב פסח (רבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about an ordinary שבת. רבי ישמעאל treats it like an ordinary weekday.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: an ordinary שבת is like an ordinary ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: In רבה בר עולא's reading, רבי עקיבא says that on an ordinary שבת the תמיד is brought earlier, like on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Like its order on a regular ערב פסח, so is its order on a regular שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues רבה בר עולא's new reading by giving רבי עקיבא's side. He says an ordinary שבת follows the earlier schedule of ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday ערב פסח the תמיד is moved up to seven and a half hours. רבי עקיבא says every שבת is like that too, because no voluntary offerings are brought on שבת, so the תמיד can come earlier. The argument is therefore only about an ordinary שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא disagreeing with רבי ישמעאל
the day before פסח, when the תמיד is moved earlier
an ordinary שבת during the year

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Like its arrangement on an ordinary Passover eve,
phrases.notes: A weekday ערב פסח, when the תמיד is at seven and a half hours.

phrases.english: so is its arrangement on an ordinary Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּסִידְרוֹ בְּעֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבה בר עולא's rereading of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, on an ordinary שבת the afternoon תמיד is brought at the earlier ערב פסח time (seven and a half hours).

steps.title: Our משנה fits everyone
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא's argument is only about an ordinary שבת, the משנה's ruling for ערב פסח, weekday or שבת, is agreed on by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה, which teaches 'whether on a weekday or on שבת', is the view of everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the result of רבה בר עולא's reading. The משנה about ערב פסח is not part of the argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבא's reading, the ברייתא's argument was about a שבת that falls on ערב פסח, so the משנה seemed to side with one view. Now the argument is moved to an ordinary שבת. So both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree that on ערב פסח the time is the same whether it falls on a weekday or on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
whether on a weekday or on שבת
the view of everyone (no argument)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה בר עולא: the ברייתא's argument is about an ordinary שבת. רבי ישמעאל says it is like an ordinary weekday; רבי עקיבא says it is like ערב פסח. The משנה about ערב פסח is דברי הכל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This move keeps the משנה from depending on one side of a מחלוקת. That is a common goal when the גמרא rereads a ברייתא.

phrases.english: And the mishna, which teaches
'whether on a weekday or on Shabbat',
is the opinion of all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְנִיתִין דְּקָתָנֵי בֵּין בַּחוֹל בֵּין בַּשַּׁבָּת דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the consequence of רבה בר עולא's rereading for our משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רבה בר עולא's reading, the משנה's single time for ערב פסח, weekday or שבת, is agreed on by both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: What is the basis of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about an ordinary שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. Now that the ברייתא has been read as an argument about an ordinary שבת, it asks what reasoning each side is using.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבה בר עולא's reading, רבי ישמעאל puts the שבת תמיד at the normal weekday time, and רבי עקיבא puts it earlier. The גמרא wants the underlying reason for this split, not just the two times.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root principle of a dispute)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: He means רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, as רבה בר עולא explains them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבה בר עולא's reading of the ברייתא and asks for the reasoning behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle explains why רבי ישמעאל keeps the weekday time on שבת while רבי עקיבא moves it earlier?

steps.title: They argue about a decree because of voluntary offerings
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is whether we make a גזירה on שבת because of the weekday. On weekdays the תמיד is pushed late to leave room for נדרים and נדבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about a decree made because of free-will offerings and vowed offerings. רבי ישמעאל holds that we decree on שבת because of the weekday. רבי עקיבא holds that we do not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי ישמעאל wants שבת to follow the weekday schedule as a safeguard, and רבי עקיבא does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday the תמיד waits until eight and a half hours, because private נדרים and נדבות must be brought before it. On שבת no private offerings are brought, so that reason does not apply. רבי ישמעאל still keeps the late time so people will not mix up the two schedules, while רבי עקיבא sees no need for this decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic safeguard decree / we make such a decree
Free-will offerings
Vowed offerings (a person obligated himself to bring them)
Because of, on account of (one case is decreed because of another)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think private offerings are brought on שבת. They are not. That is exactly why רבי ישמעאל needs a גזירה to keep the late weekday time.

phrases.english: They disagree about a decree because of free-will offerings and vowed offerings.
Rabbi Yishmael holds:
We decree on Shabbat because of the weekday,
phrases.notes: So the תמיד stays at eight and a half hours on שבת as well.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds: we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether to make a גזירה on שבת because of the weekday, when the תמיד is delayed for נדרים and נדבות.

steps.title: Then why not bring it even earlier?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא makes no decree, the תמיד should be brought at its earliest time, six and a half hours, not seven and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we do not decree, let it be brought at six and a half hours!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's position. If nothing is holding the תמיד back on שבת, why bring it at seven and a half hours instead of six and a half?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six and a half hours is the earliest possible time for the afternoon תמיד. Once the weekday delay is gone, there seems to be no reason to wait an extra hour. So the specific time of seven and a half needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us do it / let it be performed
Six and a half hours into the day, the earliest time for the afternoon תמיד

phrases.english: If we do not decree,
let it be brought at six and a half hours!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא גָּזְרִינַן, נִיעְבְּדֵיהּ בְּשֵׁשׁ וּמֶחְצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's 'no decree' position from step 8 to question his time of seven and a half hours.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's placement of the שבת תמיד at seven and a half hours
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a decree nothing delays the תמיד, so it should be at its earliest time, six and a half hours.

steps.title: The additional offerings and frankincense bowls come first
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the מוספין come before the בזיכין. The מוספין are at six hours and the בזיכין at seven, so the תמיד is at seven and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the additional offerings come before the bowls of frankincense. The additional offerings are at six hours, the bowls at seven, and the תמיד is brought at seven and a half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two other שבת services must happen first, and they take up the time until seven. This pushes the תמיד to seven and a half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the מוספין are offered, and the בזיכין of frankincense from the לחם הפנים are burned. According to רבי עקיבא the order is מוספין first, then בזיכין, and only then the תמיד. This is the same reasoning used earlier in step 2, now applied to an ordinary שבת in רבה בר עולא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (introducing someone's view)
The additional offerings brought on שבת and holidays
The bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים and burned on שבת

phrases.english: He holds: the additional offerings come before the frankincense bowls.
The additional offerings at six, and the bowls at seven,
and he brings the daily offering at seven and a half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a competing scheduling factor (the order of the שבת services)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a decree, nothing should delay the תמיד past six and a half hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מוספין at six and the בזיכין at seven must come first, so the תמיד is brought at seven and a half.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about the times of the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. All year the תמיד is slaughtered at eight and a half hours, and on ערב פסח at seven and a half. רבי ישמעאל says ערב פסח on שבת is 'like it fell on Monday,' while רבי עקיבא says it follows its ערב פסח order.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: All year the תמיד is offered by its normal rule. It is slaughtered at eight and a half hours and offered at nine and a half. On ערב פסח it is slaughtered at seven and a half and offered at eight and a half. If ערב פסח fell on שבת, it is like when it falls on Monday. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: like its order on ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא as the basis of a challenge. The next step will say whom it challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא places the dispute directly on ערב פסח that falls on שבת. רבי ישמעאל says that day is treated like ערב פסח on a Monday. This wording will turn out to match one of the earlier explanations of the dispute but not the other.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
According to its normal rule
Monday (the second day of the week)
According to its usual order / schedule

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: תָּמִיד, כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ קָרֵב כְּהִלְכָתוֹ:
phrases.english: They raised an objection: The daily offering, all year round, is offered according to its rule:

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁחָט בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה וּמֶחְצָה, וְקָרֵב בְּתֵשַׁע וּמֶחְצָה.
phrases.english: it is slaughtered at eight and a half and offered at nine and a half.
And on Passover eve, it is slaughtered at seven and a half,
and offered at eight and a half.
If it fell on Shabbat,
it is like when it falls on Monday,
phrases.notes: As written, this sounds like: ערב פסח on שבת is treated like ערב פסח on a weekday.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּסִידְרוֹ בְּעֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: like its order on Passover eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from an outside ברייתא, testing the earlier explanations of אביי and רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא places the dispute explicitly on ערב פסח that falls on שבת, using the phrase 'like when it falls on Monday.'

steps.title: This fits אביי but is hard for רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא works well with אביי's explanation but is difficult for רבא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to אביי it works out well. But according to רבא it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now names the target of the challenge from the ברייתא. It fits אביי's explanation and seems to contradict רבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אביי and רבא placed the dispute on ערב פסח that falls on שבת. They differ about רבי ישמעאל's time. For אביי it is seven and a half hours, like ערב פסח on a weekday. For רבא it is eight and a half hours, like an ordinary weekday. This ברייתא compares the day to ערב פסח on a Monday, which matches אביי and not רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side, setting up a 'but')
It works out well
It is difficult

phrases.english: Granted, according to Abaye it works out well,
but according to Rava it is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרָבָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out whom the ברייתא of step 11 challenges.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has רבי ישמעאל treat ערב פסח on שבת like ערב פסח on a Monday (seven and a half hours). That is אביי's view, while רבא had רבי ישמעאל at the ordinary weekday time (eight and a half).

steps.title: רבא rereads 'like Monday' as 'like an ordinary Monday'
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes the reading. The ברייתא does not mean 'like ערב פסח falling on Monday.' It means 'like an ordinary Monday,' so for רבי ישמעאל, ערב פסח on שבת uses the regular weekday time of eight and a half hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: Do not say 'like when it falls on Monday.' Rather say: like an ordinary Monday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by rereading one phrase in the ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל is now comparing שבת to a regular weekday, not to ערב פסח on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is still ערב פסח that falls on שבת ('חל להיות בשבת'); only רבי ישמעאל's comparison changes, to an ordinary Monday instead of ערב פסח on a Monday. So רבי ישמעאל keeps the ordinary weekday time of eight and a half hours, and רבי עקיבא keeps the usual ערב פסח time of seven and a half. That is exactly רבא's explanation, so the ברייתא no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense offered on someone's behalf)
Do not say this; rather say that (a reading adjustment)
Of the world, i.e., ordinary or regular

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits אביי as written. רבא saves his view by reading 'like Monday' as 'like an ordinary Monday.' For רבי ישמעאל, then, ערב פסח on שבת uses the regular weekday time of eight and a half hours, as רבא explained.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כְּשֵׁנִי בַּשַּׁבָּת' here means Monday, not 'like the second (time) on שבת.' שבת is used here as a name for the week.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
Do not say "like when it falls on Monday,"
rather say: like an ordinary Monday.
phrases.notes: So the תמיד is at eight and a half hours, like any normal weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty against רבא raised in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא compares ערב פסח on שבת to ערב פסח on a Monday, which contradicts רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא compares ערב פסח on שבת to an ordinary Monday (eight and a half hours) for רבי ישמעאל, which matches רבא's explanation.

steps.title: A second ברייתא about ערב פסח on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל says that when ערב פסח falls on שבת, the תמיד follows its year-round schedule. רבי עקיבא says it follows the schedule of an ordinary ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If ערב פסח fell on שבת, the תמיד is brought according to its order all year long. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: it follows its order on a regular ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to test אביי and רבא. This step only quotes the source. The next step spells out who it causes trouble for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'its order all year long' means the normal weekday time of eight and a half hours. 'A regular ערב פסח' means seven and a half hours. That reading matches how רבא explained the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא)
According to its usual order or schedule
All year long, meaning the normal weekday schedule
An ordinary ערב פסח (one that falls on a weekday)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If [ערב פסח] fell on Shabbat —
[the תמיד is] according to its order all year long,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
according to its order on an ordinary Passover eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא answered the first ברייתא, the גמרא brings a second ברייתא that leans the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation of the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain wording places רבי ישמעאל at the year-round weekday time. אביי had said רבי ישמעאל uses the ערב פסח time.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רבא but is difficult for אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this ברייתא fits רבא well but is a problem for אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבא, but for אביי it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge outright. This ברייתא supports רבא and contradicts אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that רבי ישמעאל treats this day like a regular weekday (eight and a half hours), which matches 'all year long.' אביי said רבי ישמעאל treats it like ערב פסח on Monday (seven and a half hours). The ברייתא's wording does not seem to say that.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (for one side)
It works out well
It is difficult

steps.confusionAlert: This is the mirror image of steps 11 to 13. There, the first ברייתא was hard for רבא. Here, the second ברייתא is hard for אביי.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava it works out well,
but according to Abaye it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְאַבָּיֵי קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the problem that the ברייתא from step 14 creates.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's version of רבי ישמעאל's opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'All year long' sounds like the normal weekday time. אביי had said רבי ישמעאל uses the ערב פסח time.

steps.title: אביי changes the reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads 'all years' instead of 'all year.' רבי ישמעאל says the תמיד follows the ערב פסח time of every year. רבי עקיבא says it follows the time used when ערב פסח falls on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can say to you: Do not say 'according to its order all year.' Rather, say 'according to its order in all the years.' These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: it follows the order of ערב פסח that falls on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by changing the wording of the ברייתא so that it matches his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the years' means the usual ערב פסח time every year, which is seven and a half hours. So רבי ישמעאל makes no special change for שבת. רבי עקיבא compares it to ערב פסח on Friday, which is six and a half hours, matching אביי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say this, rather say that (a change in the text's reading)
All the years, meaning the usual ערב פסח schedule each year
Friday, the day before שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא answers the ברייתא that challenges him by changing a word. רבא changed 'Monday ערב פסח' to 'ordinary Monday.' אביי changed 'all year' to 'all years.'

phrases.english: Abaye can say to you:
Do not say "according to its order all year,"
rather say:
according to its order in all the years,
phrases.notes: The usual ערב פסח time, seven and a half hours.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
according to the order of Passover eve
that falls on Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against אביי from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the reading of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא puts רבי ישמעאל at the normal weekday time, against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the new reading, רבי ישמעאל uses the usual ערב פסח time and רבי עקיבא uses the Friday ערב פסח time. Both positions match אביי.

steps.title: Nothing may come before the morning תמיד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how we know that no offering may come before the morning תמיד. It answers from the פסוק 'וערך עליה העולה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: From where do we know that nothing should come before the morning תמיד? The פסוק says: 'And he shall arrange upon it the עולה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic, prompted by the earlier point that the morning תמיד comes first. It quotes a ברייתא that gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the rule and names the פסוק, but it does not yet explain how the פסוק proves it. The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The morning daily offering
The פסוק teaches
And he shall arrange the עולה upon it (ויקרא ו:ה)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From where do we know that nothing shall
precede the daily morning offering?
The verse states:
"And he shall prepare the burnt-offering upon it."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר קוֹדֶם לְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected to the earlier statement that the morning תמיד comes before all other offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No offering may be brought before the morning תמיד.

steps.title: רבא explains the proof from the word 'העולה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק shows this. רבא answers that 'העולה' means the first עולה, which is the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the proof? רבא said: 'The עולה' means the first עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the פסוק proves the rule, and רבא answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'the' (the letter ה) points to a specific, well-known עולה, namely the first one of the day. Since the פסוק describes it as the first offering placed on the מזבח, nothing may come before it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the proof? How does the פסוק teach this?
The first עולה, meaning the morning תמיד

phrases.english: What is the derivation?
Rava said:
"The burnt-offering" means the first burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 17 proves its rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'וערך עליה העולה' shows that the morning תמיד must come first
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'the' in 'העולה' marks it as the first עולה of the day.

steps.title: Nothing may come after the afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. It asks how we know that nothing is offered after the afternoon תמיד, and answers from 'והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that nothing is offered after the afternoon תמיד? The פסוק says: 'And he shall burn upon it the fats of the שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second half of the rule, the end of the day. This sets up another question about how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the morning תמיד opens the day, the afternoon תמיד closes it. The source is the second half of the same פסוק. How it proves the rule is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon daily offering
And he shall burn (on the מזבח)
The fats of the שלמים offerings

phrases.english: And from where do we know that nothing is offered
after the daily afternoon offering?
The verse states:
"And he shall cause the fats of the peace-offerings to go up in smoke upon it."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין דָּבָר קָרֵב אַחַר תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same ברייתא, now about the end of the day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No offering may be brought after the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: אביי explains the proof from the word 'עליה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this פסוק shows the rule. אביי answers that שלמים are offered 'upon it' (after the morning תמיד), but not upon its partner, the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the proof? אביי said: Upon 'it' come שלמים, but not upon its partner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the second proof works, and אביי explains. This closes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עליה' here means 'after it.' It refers to the morning עולה mentioned just before in the פסוק. שלמים may be brought after the morning תמיד, but not after its partner, the afternoon תמיד. So nothing may follow the afternoon תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Upon it, understood here as 'after it' (after the morning תמיד)
Its partner, meaning the afternoon תמיד

steps.whatToRemember: The two תמידים bracket the day. Nothing comes before the morning תמיד (from 'העולה,' explained by רבא). Nothing comes after the afternoon תמיד (from 'עליה,' explained by אביי).

phrases.english: What is the derivation?
Abaye said:
"Upon it" peace-offerings [may be brought],
but not upon its counterpart may peace-offerings [be brought].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 19 proves its rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים' shows that nothing may follow the afternoon תמיד
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עליה' limits the שלמים to after the morning תמיד, not after its partner, the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: רבא objects: the verse only mentions peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that אביי's פסוק only forbids שלמים after the afternoon תמיד. It says nothing about עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenges this: Maybe the rule is only that we may not offer שלמים after the afternoon תמיד, but we may still offer עולות!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's proof from the previous step. The פסוק אביי used talks about 'חלבי השלמים', the fats of peace-offerings, and nothing else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learned from 'והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים' that offerings are not brought after the afternoon תמיד. But the פסוק names only שלמים. So at most it proves that שלמים may not come late, and other offerings like עולות might still be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it (a strong challenge)
Peace-offerings
Burnt-offerings (fully burned on the מזבח)
We may offer / sacrifice

phrases.english: Rava strongly objects to it:
Say it is peace-offerings that we may not offer (after the afternoon tamid),
phrases.notes: Because the verse only mentions peace-offerings.

phrases.english: but burnt-offerings we may offer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reading of the פסוק in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's proof from 'והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only names שלמים. So it cannot prove a general rule for all offerings, especially עולות.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: all offerings are completed on the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads 'השלמים' as 'השלם', meaning 'complete'. All offerings must be completed by the time of the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The word 'השלמים' should be read as 'השלם'. On it (the תמיד) complete all of the offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops אביי's approach and gives his own way to learn the rule from the same פסוק. He plays on the word 'השלמים' and reads it as 'השלם', which means 'finish'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the פסוק is no longer only about peace-offerings. It teaches a general rule: every offering of the day must be finished on, or before, the afternoon תמיד. This covers עולות too, so רבא's challenge is solved.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier approach)
Complete / finish
Upon it (the עולה, the תמיד)
All the offerings, every one of them

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the word means something other than peace-offerings in its simple meaning. He is making a דרשה, a sound-based reading, from 'השלמים' to 'השלם'.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, 'השלמים' means 'השלם': all offerings must be finished by the afternoon תמיד. Nothing at all, not even an עולה, comes after it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the afternoon תמיד closes the day's offerings. That is exactly why the ערב פסח order in the next ברייתא needs explaining.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
"Hashelamim": upon it, complete
phrases.notes: Wordplay: הַשְּׁלָמִים (peace-offerings) is read as הַשְׁלֵם (complete).

phrases.english: all of the offerings, every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own challenge from Step 21 by replacing אביי's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the same פסוק with a new דרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק speaks only of שלמים, so עולות might be allowed after the afternoon תמיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'השלמים' is read as 'השלם': all offerings must be completed by the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: The order of the afternoon service on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the order: תמיד first, then the פסח, then the קטורת, then lighting the נרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The תמיד comes before the פסח. The פסח comes before the קטורת. The קטורת comes before the lighting of the נרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives the order of the afternoon Temple service on ערב פסח. This statement opens the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the קרבן פסח is brought after the afternoon תמיד. That is an exception to the rule just learned, that nothing is offered after the afternoon תמיד. The ברייתא also places the קטורת and the lighting of the מנורה after the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Comes before / precedes
The incense burned in the היכל
The lamps of the מנורה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the פסח cancels the rule that the afternoon תמיד ends the day. It is a special exception to that rule, and the גמרא on the next amud discusses how the פסח can come after the תמיד.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The daily offering precedes the Paschal lamb,
the Paschal lamb precedes the incense,
the incense precedes the lamps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the rule that nothing comes after the afternoon תמיד, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with the ערב פסח order, where the פסח does come after it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order of the afternoon service: תמיד, then פסח, then קטורת, then נרות.
